title: Oncogenes Stuck ON: Receptor Activation, HER2, MYC and ctDNA
summary: See the three structural ways a growth factor receptor is jammed on, how the Burkitt translocation deregulates MYC, and what serum HER2 extracellular domain and plasma KRAS tumour DNA can and cannot tell the laboratory.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 76 Hits 6, 8, 9 and 12 (second lesson for Ch. 76). Checked against Du & Lovly 2018, Mishra 2017, Nahta 2012, An 2018, Wu 2022, Lee 2014, Reix 2016, Aquino 2013, Woroniecka 2022, Kinde 2011 (read via a page-fetch tool) and Cohen 2017 (read via a page-fetch tool). Discrepancies: the reviewer’s pancreatic ctDNA figures (KRAS ~10%, CA 19-9 ~30%) differ from Cohen 2017 (30% and 49%; register rv-ctdna-pancreas-sens); the HER2 “25–50% of stage III/IV, 40- to 190-fold” figure was not found, and serum ECD is normal in most tissue HER2-positive primary tumours (register rv-her2-serum-ecd); the neu valine→glutamate example is a rat mutation not found in human tumours, and reviews list further activation routes (register rv-receptor-activation-routes). Not taught: c-myc “75-kDa”, anti–c-myc antibody frequencies, the “1 in 10,000” ctDNA limit, the HGF/OPN/CEA “~65%” wording, the >15 ng/mL survival claim.

objectives: Describe three structural routes to ligand-independent receptor tyrosine kinase signalling: overexpression, extracellular-domain loss and transmembrane-domain mutation.
Explain how t(8;14) and its variants deregulate MYC in Burkitt lymphoma, and why a MYC rearrangement is not unique to Burkitt.
Interpret serum HER2 extracellular domain and plasma KRAS ctDNA results within their limits.

scenes.title: Three requests, three switches
scenes.altText: Invented scenario: three requests reach a molecular oncology bench — (1) serum HER2 extracellular domain (ECD) for a woman with metastatic, tissue HER2-positive breast cancer; (2) MYC break-apart FISH on a lymph node with a very high proliferation rate; (3) plasma KRAS circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) for a patient with a resectable pancreatic mass. Question token: “What is each test really seeing?”

cues.text: Three requests reach the molecular bench: a serum HER2 level for a woman with metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer, and MYC testing on a fast-growing lymphoma.
The third is a plasma test for KRAS tumour DNA in a patient with a small pancreatic mass.
Each test looks at an oncogene that has been switched on. What is each one really seeing?

props.label: What is each test really seeing?

scenes.title: How the switch normally works
scenes.altText: Schematic receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK): extracellular ligand-binding domain, a single transmembrane helix, and an intracellular tyrosine kinase domain. Normally, ligand binding induces receptor dimerization; the kinases trans-phosphorylate the C-terminal tails and signal onward (for ErbB receptors, dimerization is receptor-mediated through an exposed dimerization arm). Without ligand, the ErbB extracellular region is held in a tethered, autoinhibited shape. Second card: MYC (c-Myc) is a transcription factor encoded at 8q24 that works by dimerizing with MAX.

cues.text: A growth factor receptor has three parts: an outside ligand-binding domain, a single helix crossing the membrane, and a tyrosine kinase inside the cell.
Normally the receptor is quiet until its ligand arrives. Ligand binding brings two receptors together, and the paired kinases phosphorylate each other and pass the signal on.
In the ErbB family, which includes EGFR and HER2, the outside region stays folded shut until ligand opens a dimerization arm.
A different kind of oncogene is MYC, a transcription factor encoded on chromosome 8 at band q24. It acts as a pair with its partner protein, MAX.

scenes.title: Stuck in the ON position
scenes.altText: Three structural routes to ligand-independent receptor signalling. (1) Overexpression, most often from gene amplification (ERBB2/HER2, EGFR, MET): a higher local receptor concentration drives excess signalling. (2) Loss of the extracellular domain: EGFRvIII (deletion of exons 2–7) lacks the ligand-binding domain and is constitutively active, with weak kinase activity. (3) Transmembrane-domain point mutation: rat neu V664E (valine → glutamic acid) makes the kinase constitutively active and supports dimerization; not found in human tumours, but human HER2 transmembrane mutations V659E and G660D drive some lung adenocarcinomas. Note: reviews list four principal routes overall (gain-of-function mutation, amplification, rearrangement, autocrine activation). MYC card: in Burkitt lymphoma, t(8;14)(q24;q32) places MYC next to the IGH enhancer, causing overexpression; variants t(2;8) (IGK) and t(8;22) (IGL); MYC rearrangement also occurs in 5–10% of diffuse large B-cell lymphomas.

cues.text: Cancer can jam a receptor on in three structural ways. First, too many copies: gene amplification of HER2, EGFR or MET crowds the membrane with receptors, and signalling overwhelms the brakes.
Second, lose the outside domain. The glioblastoma variant EGFR-v-three lacks its ligand-binding domain and signals constantly, though weakly.

Third, a point mutation in the membrane helix. In the rat neu gene, valine 664 changed to glutamic acid jams the kinase on. That exact change is not seen in human tumours, but similar HER2 helix mutations drive some lung cancers.

MYC is switched on differently. In Burkitt lymphoma, the translocation between chromosomes 8 and 14 parks MYC next to the immunoglobulin heavy-chain enhancer, so it is overexpressed. Variants use the kappa or lambda light-chain genes, and MYC rearrangements also occur in other aggressive B-cell lymphomas.

scenes.title: What blood tests can and cannot see
scenes.altText: HER2 card: HER2 is a 185-kDa receptor; its ECD can be shed into serum, leaving a truncated, constitutively active p95 fragment in the membrane. Serum ECD >15 ng/mL is the most-used cutoff; elevated in about 4–10% of early-stage and 20–80% of metastatic breast cancers. In 2,862 primary breast cancers, 4.4% had elevated serum ECD, and only about 15% of tissue HER2-positive tumours did — tissue IHC/ISH defines HER2 status; serum ECD is studied for prognosis and monitoring. ctDNA card: Safe-SeqS tags each template molecule with a unique identifier (UID); a mutation shared by ≥95% of a UID family (a “supermutant”) is real, separating true rare mutations from sequencing errors. In 221 resectable pancreatic cancers (Cohen 2017): KRAS ctDNA 30%, CA 19-9 49%, combined 60%, plus four proteins 64%; 1 of 182 controls positive. Hook answers card.

cues.text: HER2 is a 185-kilodalton receptor whose outside domain can be shed into serum. Serum levels above 15 nanograms per millilitre are the usual cutoff: raised in a minority of early breast cancers, and more often in metastatic disease.
In one series of nearly three thousand primary breast cancers, only about fifteen percent of tissue HER2-positive tumours had a raised serum level. Tissue testing defines HER2 status.

Tumour DNA in plasma can be vanishingly rare. Molecular barcodes tag every original DNA molecule, so a mutation shared by a whole barcode family is real, while a random sequencing error is not. In resectable pancreatic cancer, KRAS tumour DNA alone was found in thirty percent; with CA 19-9, sixty percent.

Back to the hook. Serum HER2 tracks the tumour, but tissue decides HER2 status. MYC testing finds a rearrangement, which is not unique to Burkitt. And plasma KRAS alone misses most resectable pancreatic cancers.

props.label: Hook: track · not unique · misses most

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “Normal serum HER2 ECD means the tumour is HER2-negative” (✓ most tissue HER2-positive primary tumours have normal serum ECD; tissue IHC/ISH defines status); “A MYC rearrangement proves Burkitt lymphoma” (✓ MYC rearrangements also occur in 5–10% of DLBCL and other aggressive B-cell lymphomas); “Plasma KRAS ctDNA alone detects most early pancreatic cancers” (✓ 30% of resectable cases; 60–64% only when combined with protein markers).

cues.text: Trap one: a normal serum HER2 means a HER2-negative tumour. No: most tissue HER2-positive primary tumours have normal serum levels. Tissue decides.
Trap two: a MYC rearrangement proves Burkitt lymphoma. No: MYC rearrangements also occur in other aggressive B-cell lymphomas.
Trap three: plasma KRAS alone catches most early pancreatic cancers. No: about thirty percent alone, and around sixty percent only when combined with protein markers.

props.title: ✗ “MYC rearranged = Burkitt.”
lines: ✓ Also in DLBCL and other lymphomas

scenes.title: Crowd, cut, kink, move
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “A receptor jams ON when it is CROWDED (overexpression), CUT (outside domain lost) or KINKED (membrane-helix mutation); MYC jams ON when it MOVES next to the immunoglobulin loudspeaker (IG enhancer).” Tokens: crowd · cut · kink · move. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: a receptor jams on when it is crowded, cut or kinked: too many copies, a lost outside domain, or a mutation in the membrane helix. MYC jams on when it moves next to the immunoglobulin loudspeaker.

Where it breaks: kinase-domain mutations, gene fusions and autocrine loops also activate receptors; the classic valine-to-glutamate change is in rat neu, not human tumours; and MYC can also partner with the light-chain genes.

props.title: Where it breaks
lines: Kinase mutations, fusions, autocrine loops too
V664E is rat neu, not human
MYC also pairs with IGK or IGL

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “Receptors jam ON by amplification, loss of the outside domain or a membrane-helix mutation; MYC by moving next to an IG enhancer”, “Serum HER2 does not define HER2 status · MYC rearrangement is not unique to Burkitt · KRAS ctDNA alone misses most early pancreatic cancers”.

cues.text: Oncogenes are jammed on by receptor amplification, loss of the outside domain, membrane-helix mutation or MYC moving next to an immunoglobulin enhancer, yet blood tests only partly see them, because tissue still defines HER2 status and plasma KRAS alone misses most early pancreatic cancers.

props.label: Crowd · cut · kink (receptors) · move (MYC → IG enhancer)
Tissue defines HER2 · MYC ≠ only Burkitt · KRAS ctDNA alone ~30%

explanation.what: Plain language: oncogenes are normal growth switches stuck in the ON position. A receptor can be stuck on because there are too many copies, because its outside part is missing, or because its membrane anchor is mutated; MYC is stuck on when a chromosome swap puts it next to an antibody-gene enhancer. Blood tests can pick up shed receptor fragments or tumour DNA, but only some of the time. Scientific terms: receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK), ligand-induced dimerization, gene amplification, EGFRvIII, transmembrane domain (TMD), neu V664E, HER2 (p185, ERBB2) extracellular domain (ECD), p95HER2, t(8;14)(q24;q32), IGH/IGK/IGL enhancers, circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA), unique identifier (UID), Safe-SeqS, supermutant.
explanation.why: Ligand-independent dimerization or excess receptor number keeps kinases signalling; juxtaposition of MYC to an immunoglobulin enhancer drives overexpression in B cells. Serum HER2 ECD is more often raised in metastatic than in early disease, and ctDNA is less often detectable at earlier stages, so blood tests miss many early or tissue-positive cases.
explanation.measure: Serum HER2 ECD: cutoff usually 15 ng/mL; elevated in ~4–10% of early and 20–80% of metastatic breast cancers; 4.4% of 2,862 primary cancers, ~15% of tissue HER2-positive ones. Tissue HER2 by IHC with ISH for equivocal (2+) cases. ctDNA: UID families separate true mutations from sequencing errors; resectable pancreatic cancer (n = 221): KRAS 30%, CA 19-9 49%, combined 60%, five-marker panel 64%, 1 of 182 controls positive.
explanation.differs: Overexpression (more normal receptors) vs ECD loss (EGFRvIII) vs TMD point mutation (neu V664E; human HER2 V659E/G660D); t(8;14) IGH vs variant t(2;8) IGK and t(8;22) IGL; serum ECD (prognosis/monitoring) vs tissue IHC/ISH (HER2 status); ctDNA alone vs combined with protein markers.
explanation.examAngle: Expect: match EGFRvIII or neu V664E to its mechanism, identify the partner gene in t(8;14), recognise that MYC rearrangement also occurs outside Burkitt, decide that tissue rather than serum defines HER2 status, or recognise that KRAS ctDNA alone has limited sensitivity for early pancreatic cancer.

mnemonic.text: A receptor jams ON when it is CROWDED (overexpression), CUT (outside domain lost) or KINKED (membrane-helix mutation); MYC jams ON when it MOVES next to the immunoglobulin loudspeaker (IG enhancer).
mnemonic.explanation: Crowd, cut, kink = the three structural receptor routes; move = MYC translocation to an IG locus.

analogyLimitations: Receptor and chromosome drawings are schematic.
Serum HER2 and ctDNA figures come from single studies or one meta-analysis; assays and cohorts differ.
takeaway: Oncogenes are jammed on by receptor amplification, loss of the outside domain, membrane-helix mutation or MYC moving next to an immunoglobulin enhancer, yet blood tests only partly see them, because tissue still defines HER2 status and plasma KRAS alone misses most early pancreatic cancers.

questions.stem: EGFRvIII, found in glioblastoma, lacks exons 2–7 and signals without ligand. Which mechanism of receptor activation does it illustrate?

options.text: Loss of the extracellular ligand-binding domain
options.rationale: Correct. EGFRvIII has no ligand-binding domain and is constitutively active, although its kinase activity is weak.
Incorrect. Amplification raises the number of otherwise normal receptors; EGFRvIII is a structurally altered receptor.

options.text: A valine-to-glutamate point mutation in the transmembrane helix
options.rationale: Incorrect. That describes rat neu V664E, a transmembrane-domain mutation.

options.text: Translocation next to an immunoglobulin enhancer
options.rationale: Incorrect. That is how MYC is deregulated in Burkitt lymphoma, not how EGFR is activated.

questions.stem: Karyotyping of a Burkitt lymphoma shows t(8;14)(q24;q32). What is the main consequence of this translocation?

options.text: MYC is placed next to the immunoglobulin heavy-chain enhancer and is overexpressed
options.rationale: Correct. Juxtaposition of MYC (8q24) to IGH (14q32) enhancer elements drives MYC overexpression.
Incorrect. EGFR amplification is a receptor-overexpression route; t(8;14) moves MYC next to IGH.

options.text: MYC is deleted, removing a growth brake
options.rationale: Incorrect. In Burkitt lymphoma MYC is overexpressed after juxtaposition to an IG enhancer, not deleted.

options.text: The kappa light-chain gene is joined to MYC
options.rationale: Incorrect. Kappa (IGK, 2p11) is the partner in the variant t(2;8); t(8;14) involves IGH.

questions.stem: A patient with a primary breast cancer that is HER2-positive by tissue IHC has a serum HER2 extracellular domain of 9 ng/mL (cutoff 15 ng/mL). What is the best interpretation?

options.text: The tissue result stands; serum ECD is normal in most tissue HER2-positive primary tumours
options.rationale: Correct. In a series of 2,862 primary breast cancers, only about 15% of tissue HER2-positive tumours had raised serum ECD; tissue IHC/ISH defines HER2 status.
Incorrect. Tissue IHC/ISH, not serum ECD, determines HER2 status, and serum ECD was raised in only about 15% of tissue HER2-positive primary tumours.

options.text: The serum assay must have failed
options.rationale: Incorrect. A normal serum level is common in early or tissue-positive disease and does not imply assay failure.

options.text: The normal level proves there is no metastatic disease
options.rationale: Incorrect. Serum ECD is raised in only a proportion (about 20–80% across studies) of metastatic breast cancers.

claims.text: RTK structure, ligand-induced dimerization, ErbB tethered ECD; overexpression via amplification.
EGFRvIII lacks exons 2–7 and the ligand-binding domain; constitutively active, weak kinase.
Rat neu V664E valine→glutamic acid TMD mutation, constitutively active, not found in human tumours; human HER2 V659E/G660D TMD drivers in NSCLC; four principal mechanisms overall.

MYC transcription factor at 8q24 dimerizing with MAX; t(8;14) IGH most frequent in BL; variants t(2;8) IGK and t(8;22) IGL; juxtaposition to IG enhancers causes overexpression; MYC rearrangement in 5–10% of DLBCL.
HER2 185 kDa; ECD shedding and p95; 15 ng/mL cutoff; 4–10% early vs 20–80% metastatic; 4.4% of primary and ~15% of tissue-positive tumours elevated; tissue IHC/ISH defines status.
Safe-SeqS UIDs and supermutants; pancreatic ctDNA and protein-marker sensitivities and control specificity.
c-myc “75-kDa”; anti–c-myc antibodies in 55–65% of colorectal cancers; ctDNA “1 mutant in 10,000” limit; HER2 “25–50% of stage III/IV at 40- to 190-fold”; drop below 15 ng/mL and survival.
claims.note: Not taught as facts in this lesson; not found in the sources read.

claims.text: Scenario invented; receptor and chromosome drawings schematic.

accuracyFlags.issue: The reviewer gives pancreatic KRAS ctDNA ~10% and CA 19-9 ~30% sensitivity combining to >60%. Cohen 2017 (221 resectable cancers) reported KRAS ctDNA 30%, CA 19-9 49%, combined 60% and a five-marker panel 64%; the lesson teaches the study figures.

The reviewer states 25–50% of stage III/IV breast cancers have serum HER2 40- to 190-fold above normal; this was not found in the sources read. A meta-analysis reports ECD >15 ng/mL in 20–80% of metastatic and 4–10% of early cancers, and only ~15% of tissue HER2-positive primary tumours have raised serum ECD, so serum ECD does not define HER2 status.

The reviewer’s three receptor-oncogenesis mechanisms are structural routes only; reviews list four principal mechanisms (gain-of-function mutation, amplification, chromosomal rearrangement, autocrine activation), and the neu valine→glutamate example (V664E) is a rat mutation not found in human tumours, while human HER2 TMD mutations (V659E, G660D) occur in lung adenocarcinoma.
